en: n. a feeling of respect and approval for someone or something; something that you admire
ex: She spoke of her teacher with great admiration.
她以極大的敬佩之情談到她的老師。

en: n. permission to enter a place or join an organization; the price you pay to enter a place; a statement that something is true, often something bad; the act of accepting someone into a school or hospital
ex: Admission to the museum is free on Sundays.
星期日參觀博物館免費。

en: vt. to take someone else's child into your family and become its legal parent; to begin to use a new idea, method or policy; to formally accept a plan or proposal
ex: The couple adopted a baby girl last year.
那對夫妻去年收養了一名女嬰。

en: a. ready to attack or fight; determined and forceful; (of a business or style) very active in trying to win or achieve something
ex: The dog became aggressive when strangers approached.
陌生人靠近時，那隻狗變得有攻擊性。

en: a. quick to notice and react; fully aware of something dangerous or important; n. a warning of danger; vt. to warn someone about something
ex: The guard stayed alert all night.
警衛整晚保持警覺。

en: a. having more than one possible meaning; not clear or definite; not easy to understand
ex: His answer was ambiguous, and nobody knew what he meant.
他的回答模稜兩可，沒人知道他的意思。

en: a. having a strong desire to be successful or powerful; needing great effort or skill to achieve
ex: He is an ambitious young man who wants to become a CEO.
他是個雄心勃勃的年輕人，想當執行長。

en: n. a careful study of something to understand it; the process of separating something into parts to study it; a medical test
ex: The analysis of the data took several weeks.
資料分析花了好幾週。

en: vt. to study something carefully in order to understand it; to separate something into its parts to study it; to examine something using scientific methods
ex: Scientists analyzed samples of the water.
科學家分析了水的樣本。

en: n. a person in your family who lived a long time ago; an early form of an animal or plant from which later forms have developed
ex: His ancestors came from China over a hundred years ago.
他的祖先一百多年前從中國來的。

en: vt. to make someone slightly angry; to bother or disturb someone repeatedly
ex: Loud chewing really annoys me.
大聲咀嚼真的會惹惱我。

en: n. a statement that you are sorry for something you have done; a statement that explains or defends something; a poor substitute for something
ex: He made a public apology for his rude remarks.
他為自己無禮的言論公開道歉。

en: n. a person who formally asks for a job, a place at school or university, or a loan
ex: There were over a hundred applicants for the position.
這個職位有超過一百位應徵者。

en: n. a formal request for something such as a job or a loan; the use of something for a particular purpose; a computer program for a particular use; the act of putting something on a surface
ex: Please fill out the application form carefully.
請仔細填寫申請表。

en: vt. to choose someone officially for a job or position; to arrange or decide a time or place for something; vi. (appointment) the act of choosing someone for a job; an arrangement to meet someone at a particular time
ex: She was appointed as the new director of the museum.
她被任命為博物館的新館長。

en: a. suitable or right for a particular situation, person or purpose; vt. to take something for your own use without permission
ex: Wear clothes that are appropriate for the occasion.
請穿著適合場合的服裝。

en: n. a feeling or opinion that something is good or acceptable; official permission for something; agreement to a plan
ex: The plan needs approval from the board.
這項計畫需要董事會批准。

en: n. weapons used in war; the parts of the body between the shoulders and hands; the design on a shield that represents a family or institution
ex: The country has been banned from buying arms from other nations.
該國被禁止向其他國家購買武器。

en: a. made by people instead of occurring naturally; not sincere or natural; not originally from that place
ex: The cake contains artificial colors and flavors.
這個蛋糕含有人工色素和香料。

en: a. feeling embarrassed or guilty about something you have done; unwilling to do something because of shame
ex: She was ashamed of her bad behavior.
她為自己的不良行為感到羞愧。

en: n. a group of people who meet together for a particular purpose; the process of putting together the parts of something; a group of lawmakers; a part of a machine put together
ex: The school assembly starts at eight every morning.
學校的朝會每天早上八點開始。

en: vt. to give someone a job or task; to give someone something as a share; to choose someone for a position; n. (assignment) a piece of work given to a person as part of their studies or job
ex: The teacher assigned a new homework to the class.
老師給全班指派了新作業。

en: n. help or support given to someone; the act of helping someone do something; money or supplies given to people in need
ex: Do you need any assistance with your bags?
你的行李需要幫忙嗎？

en: n. a person you work with or are connected with in business; a member of an organization; vt. to connect someone or something in your mind with something else; vi. to spend time with someone
ex: He is a business associate of my father's.
他是我父親的商業夥伴。

en: n. a promise that something will definitely happen or is true; confidence in your own abilities; a kind of insurance, especially life insurance
ex: She gave me her assurance that the work would be done on time.
她向我保證工作會按時完成。

en: vt. to tell someone confidently that something is true; to make someone feel certain; to make something certain to happen
ex: I assure you that the product is safe to use.
我向你保證這項產品使用上是安全的。

en: n. the smallest part of an element that has all the chemical properties of that element; a very small amount of something; atomic energy
ex: Everything in the universe is made of atoms.
宇宙中的一切都是由原子組成的。

en: a. relating to atoms or their energy; relating to the smallest unit of a substance; (of a weapon) using atomic energy
ex: The country was devastated by the atomic bomb.
那個國家被原子彈摧毀了。

en: n. a feeling of being interested in or liking someone or something; something that people find interesting; the force that pulls things together
ex: The Eiffel Tower is a major tourist attraction.
艾菲爾鐵塔是主要的觀光景點。

en: a. relating to sound that is heard, especially recorded or broadcast sound; n. sound that is recorded or broadcast
ex: You need to turn on the audio to hear the video.
你需要開啟音訊才聽得到影片。

en: a. real and not copied or false; true and reliable; (of a document) known to be genuine
ex: The museum has an authentic painting by Picasso.
博物館有一幅畢卡索的真跡。

en: n. the power to give orders and make decisions; a person or group with official power; an expert in a particular subject; permission to do something
ex: The police have the authority to stop and search vehicles.
警方有權攔檢並搜查車輛。

en: n. the story of someone's life written by that person
ex: She published her autobiography at the age of eighty.
她八十歲時出版了自傳。

en: n. a famous person's signature; a handwritten copy of something; vt. to write your name on something, especially for a fan
ex: The actor signed an autograph for every fan.
演員為每位粉絲簽名。

en: vt. to wait for something or someone; to be going to happen to someone in the future; vi. to wait for something to happen
ex: We are awaiting your reply with interest.
我們很期待你的回覆。

en: a. having little or no hair on the head; (of a tire) with no pattern; plain and direct; vi. to lose your hair
ex: He went bald when he was only thirty.
他才三十歲就禿頭了。

en: n. something that stops people from entering a place; something that makes progress difficult or impossible; a fence or wall that stops people from going past
ex: The language barrier made communication difficult.
語言障礙使溝通變得困難。

en: n. a person who lives by asking people for money or food; a very poor person; vt. to make someone very poor
ex: A beggar sat outside the station with a cup.
一名乞丐拿著杯子坐在車站外。

en: n. a container for storing or collecting things such as grain or waste; a large container with a lid; (British) a trash can
ex: She threw the old newspapers into the bin.
她把舊報紙丟進垃圾桶。

en: n. an account of someone's life written by another person
ex: I read a biography of Albert Einstein last month.
我上個月讀了一本愛因斯坦的傳記。
